conclusions: Strong-anchor-0 and independent-four-0 meet both milestones and every retained public/probe and private case.

Sequential-four-1 and independent-four-1 meet both visible milestone gates but fail final private acceptance. Their recorded failures are inherited typed-validation regressions; both pass every private exchange and settlement scenario in this frozen suite.

Both completed-but-failed runs share list/dict nested-operation handling that raises an unexpected exception before typed validation. Sequential-four-1 additionally dereferences top-level null/list commands before validation.

Sequential-four-0 is bounded incomplete after one accepted milestone. Its retained second-milestone source fails two reviewer-generated public probes as well as three private cases. It is not another visibly accepted false completion.

The evidence distinguishes reaching a visible milestone from preserving the full inherited contract. It does not establish a causal advantage of independent generation, sequential revision, gossip transport, or any model family.

confirmed: Selected export bytes and trajectory source consistency
independent_read_only_review.scope: Two visibly completed but private-failed selected finals

metric_cautions: All five private evaluations use the same 78 scenarios. Their visible suites contain the same 41 frozen public scenarios plus different generated probes, so visible case totals are not matched challenges.

The 13 requirement groups are unequally sized: one baseline-regressions group covers 48 private predecessor scenarios; seven exchange groups cover 14 scenarios and five settlement groups cover 16. A 12/13 group score is not 12/13 uniformly sampled functionality.
Counts refer to scenario-level equality. A single failed scenario can contain several mismatched command responses; scenario counts, mismatched commands and distinct root causes are different units.
Passing all retained new-feature scenarios does not prove full new-feature correctness. Static follow-ups below were not executed and do not alter primary scores.
Two repetitions for each matched cheap policy and one strong anchor on one calendar project are insufficient for general rankings or causal effects.
purpose: Post hoc interpretation of the five primary selected calendar sources and their completed receipts; no candidate execution or changed scientific evaluation.
